original_question: Do there exist finitely generated left-orderable groups with only one nontrivial conjugacy class? A positive answer to this question implies a positive answer to 21.78. Note that D. Osin constructed torsion-free finitely generated groups with only one nontrivial conjugacy class; see 9.10 in Archive.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.80 (Y. Lodha, A. Navas) in the 'New Problems (21st issue, 2026)' portion of arXiv:1401.0300.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim: it asks for a finitely generated left-orderable group with only one nontrivial conjugacy class, and it also preserves the two contextual remarks printed immediately under the problem in the paper (the implication to 21.78 and the note about Osin's torsion-free finitely generated examples).
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, specify that 'left-orderable' means that the group admits a total order invariant under left multiplication.
Spell out 'only one nontrivial conjugacy class' as: the conjugacy classes are exactly {1} and G\{1}, equivalently every two nonidentity elements are conjugate.
State the existential quantifier explicitly in terms of a group G.
If the references to '21.78' and '9.10 in Archive' are retained, explain them as background rather than as part of the formal mathematical question; otherwise omit them from the refined question.
refined_question: Does there exist a finitely generated group G that admits a left-invariant total order and has exactly two conjugacy classes, namely {1} and G \ {1} (equivalently, every two nonidentity elements of G are conjugate)?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 21.80 exactly. In the paper, the formal problem is the single existence question about finitely generated left-orderable groups with one nontrivial conjugacy class; the subsequent sentences about Problem 21.78 and Osin's construction are contextual commentary attached to that problem, not extra hypotheses. Therefore the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is to keep the existence question unchanged in scope while unpacking the two phrases that otherwise rely on shared group-theoretic background.
